b2-mediatortenet-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Kossuth's Pesti Hírlap
b2-mediatortenet-01.scenario: At a press-history exhibition in Budapest, a visiting student asks you what the Pesti Hírlap changed in Hungarian journalism.
b2-mediatortenet-01.prompt: Tell her which genre Kossuth made central in 1841 and give your source for the subscriber figures.
cues: Say what the leading articles demanded
Name the source of the subscriber figures
b2-mediatortenet-01.target: Kossuth a Pesti Hírlap első oldalán vezércikkekben követelte a közteherviselést. A nyomdai kimutatások szerint az előfizetők száma néhány hónap alatt ötezer fölé emelkedett.
b2-mediatortenet-01.english: On the front page of the Pesti Hírlap, Kossuth demanded universal taxation in his leading articles. According to printing records, the number of subscribers rose above five thousand within a few months.
b2-mediatortenet-01.canDo: I can explain how Lajos Kossuth revolutionized Hungarian journalism with Pesti Hírlap in 1841.

b2-mediatortenet-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Talking Newspaper
b2-mediatortenet-02.scenario: At a press-history exhibition in Budapest, a visiting student asks you how the Telefonhírmondó worked and how the citizens of Budapest reacted to it.
b2-mediatortenet-02.prompt: Tell her how the news reached the subscribers and pass on, as hearsay, how some café regulars reacted at first.
cues: Say how the news reached the subscribers
Say what some regulars thought, as hearsay
b2-mediatortenet-02.target: A Telefonhírmondó telefonvezetéken keresztül közvetített híreket és műsorokat az előfizetőknek. Úgy hírlik, hogy egyes törzsvendégek kezdetben bűvészmutatványnak tartották a fülhallgatót.
b2-mediatortenet-02.english: The Telefonhírmondó transmitted news and programmes to its subscribers over telephone lines. Word has it that some regulars at first took the earpiece for a magic trick.
b2-mediatortenet-02.canDo: I can describe how the Telefonhírmondó, Tivadar Puskás's idea, worked in Budapest from 1893.

b2-mediatortenet-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Radio and Television
b2-mediatortenet-03.scenario: At a press-history exhibition in Budapest, a visiting student asks you which moments of radio and television history mattered most.
b2-mediatortenet-03.prompt: Tell her what Hungarian Television broadcast live on 16 June 1989 and what the signs in the late 1980s pointed to.
cues: Say what was broadcast live and when
Say what the signs pointed to
b2-mediatortenet-03.target: A Magyar Televízió 1989. június 16-án egyenes adásban közvetítette Nagy Imre újratemetését. Minden jel arra mutatott, hogy az állampárti tájékoztatási monopólium megrepedt.
b2-mediatortenet-03.english: On 16 June 1989 Hungarian Television broadcast Imre Nagy's reburial live. Every sign pointed to the fact that the state-party information monopoly had cracked.
b2-mediatortenet-03.canDo: I can explain the historical role of Hungarian Radio (1925, 1956) and Hungarian Television (1957, 1989).

b2-mediatortenet-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Media Law of 1996
b2-mediatortenet-04.scenario: At a press-history exhibition in Budapest, a visiting student asks you what changed in Hungarian broadcasting in the 1990s.
b2-mediatortenet-04.prompt: Tell her what the 1996 media law created and what you think explains the success of the new channels, without stating it as certain.
cues: Give a likely reason, not a certainty
b2-mediatortenet-04.target: Az 1996-os médiatörvény megteremtette a duális médiarendszert, 1997 őszén pedig elindult a TV2 és az RTL Klub. Az új csatornák valószínűleg azért tudtak milliós közönséget elhódítani, mert dinamikus híradókat adtak.
b2-mediatortenet-04.english: The 1996 media law created the dual media system, and in autumn 1997 TV2 and RTL Klub started. The new channels probably won an audience of millions because they offered dynamic news programmes.
b2-mediatortenet-04.canDo: I can analyze the transformation of the Hungarian press after 1989, including the 1990s 'media war' and the 1996 dual broadcasting law.

b2-mediatortenet-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Rumour or Fact?
b2-mediatortenet-05.scenario: At a press-history exhibition in Budapest, a visiting student asks you how a careful reader should handle news on social media.
b2-mediatortenet-05.prompt: Tell her what some surveys say about echo chambers and what a careful reader does when a page reports a rumour.
cues: Name the source of the claim about echo chambers
Say what a careful reader checks
b2-mediatortenet-05.target: Médiafogyasztási felmérések szerint a felhasználók egy része zárt véleménybuborékokban tájékozódik. Ha egy oldalon úgy hírlik valami, a tudatos olvasó megnézi, megjelölték-e a hír eredeti forrását.
b2-mediatortenet-05.english: According to media consumption surveys, some users get their information in closed echo chambers. If word has it on a page that something happened, the aware reader checks whether the original source of the news is named.
b2-mediatortenet-05.canDo: I can trace the rise of Hungarian online journalism since the late 1990s and analyze the challenges of algorithmic echo chambers.

b2-mediatortenet-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: From Pesti Hírlap to the Portals
b2-mediatortenet-consolidation.scenario: At a press-history exhibition in Budapest, a visiting student asks you how Hungarian media developed from Kossuth's time to today.
b2-mediatortenet-consolidation.prompt: Give her three dates from the history of Hungarian media and say what the signs point to today.
cues: Give three milestones with their years
Say what the signs point to today
b2-mediatortenet-consolidation.target: A Pesti Hírlap 1841-ben, a Telefonhírmondó 1893-ban indult, a Magyar Rádió pedig 1925-ben kezdte meg a rendszeres adást. Minden jel arra mutat, hogy ma az internet a legfontosabb hírforrás.
b2-mediatortenet-consolidation.english: The Pesti Hírlap started in 1841, the Telefonhírmondó in 1893, and Hungarian Radio began regular broadcasting in 1925. Every sign points to the fact that today the internet is the most important source of news.
b2-mediatortenet-consolidation.canDo: I can trace the key milestones of Hungarian media history from Kossuth's Pesti Hírlap (1841) and Puskás's Telefonhírmondó (1893) to radio, television, and digital portals.
